key_insight: The paper documents a marked increase in suspicion and scrutiny over the use of generative AI in academic manuscripts, showing this trend is reshaping editorial practices and author behavior.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of rising, often poorly calibrated suspicion about generative-AI use in scholarly submissions—its causes, consequences, and the gaps in current editorial and detection practices.
method: Analysis of publication records, editorial notices, and public cases to quantify trends in AI-related suspicion and responses
Survey/interview data from editors, reviewers and authors (and/or review of journal policies) to identify drivers and impacts of suspicion
Assessment of detection tools and policy frameworks to evaluate accuracy, false positive risks and governance shortcomings
impact: Flags urgent risks to fair peer review and academic careers, urging practitioners and publishers to adopt evidence-based policies, clearer disclosure norms, and more reliable detection/verification methods to protect research integrity.
visual_elements: Timeline chart showing rise in reported AI-suspicion incidents, editorial notices, and policy changes over time
Flow diagram of the submission → review → suspicion → editorial decision pathway highlighting pain points and false-positive risk
Bar or pie chart comparing types of editorial responses (rejection, correction, investigation, policy update)
Checklist-style icon graphic summarizing recommended practices for authors, reviewers, and journals (disclosure, verification, appeals)
paper_title: On the troubling rise of generative AI suspicion in academic publishing
